questions.q: In comparing the Early Church in Acts 2:42 to a healthy Christian church today, what core activities must present-day churches continuously devote themselves to?
options: Apostles' teaching, fellowship, breaking of bread, and prayers
Political debates, financial investments, and entertainment
Only secret prayer meetings without public worship
Isolating themselves from all community activities
questions.explain: Acts 2:42 highlights the four foundational pillars of early church life: "And they devoted themselves to the apostles' teaching and the fellowship, to the breaking of bread and the prayers." These remain the standard for modern churches.

questions.q: After King Herod killed James the brother of John, what motivated him to proceed to arrest Peter as well? (Acts 12:3)
options: Peter had stolen the king's treasury.
He saw that the execution of James pleased the Jews.
Peter threatened to overthrow his government.
An angel instructed Herod to do so.
questions.explain: Herod was driven by political favor. Acts 12:3 states: "And when he saw that it pleased the Jews, he proceeded to arrest Peter also. This was during the days of Unleavened Bread."

questions.q: When the Holy Spirit was poured out on the Day of Pentecost, some mockers accused the believers of being drunk on new wine. How did Peter logically counter this accusation in Acts 2:15?
options: By proving there was no wine stored in the upper room
By pointing out that it was only the third hour of the day (9:00 AM)
By showing them empty water jars
By having a Roman doctor examine them
questions.explain: Peter stood up and said, "For these people are not drunk, as you suppose, since it is only the third hour of the day" (which corresponds to 9:00 AM, an unlikely time for public drunkenness in that culture).

questions.q: In his Pentecost sermon, Peter explained the outpouring of the Holy Spirit by quoting an Old Testament prophet who said, "And in the last days it shall be, God declares, that I will pour out my Spirit on all flesh..." Which prophet did Peter quote? (Acts 2:16)
options: Isaiah
Jeremiah
Joel
Ezekiel
questions.explain: Peter specifically identified the source of his quotation: "But this is what was uttered through the prophet Joel..." (Acts 2:16, quoting Joel 2:28).

questions.q: When the crowd heard Peter's Pentecost speech, they were "cut to the heart" and asked what they should do. What did Peter tell them? (Acts 2:38)
options: "Go home and wait for another sign from heaven."
"Repent and be baptized every one of you in the name of Jesus Christ for the forgiveness of your sins."
"Bring all your money and give it to the apostles."
"Flee from Jerusalem before the Romans destroy it."
questions.explain: Peter replied directly to their conviction: "Repent and be baptized every one of you in the name of Jesus Christ for the forgiveness of your sins, and you will receive the gift of the Holy Spirit."

questions.q: Who was the highly respected Pharisee and teacher of the law in the Jewish council that advised them to release the apostles, warning them not to "be found opposing God"? (Acts 5:34-39)
options: Nicodemus
Joseph of Arimathea
Caiaphas
Gamaliel
questions.explain: Gamaliel, a teacher of the law held in honor by all the people, advised the council: "...keep away from these men and let them alone, for if this plan or this undertaking is of man, it will fail; but if it is of God, you will not be able to overthrow them."

questions.q: In Acts 3:1-10, Peter and John encountered a man who had been lame from birth. Where exactly was this man placed daily to ask for alms?
options: At the city gates of Jericho
At the Beautiful Gate of the temple
By the Pool of Bethesda
In the marketplace of Jerusalem
questions.explain: Acts 3:2 says: "And a man lame from birth was being carried, whom they laid daily at the gate of the temple that is called the Beautiful Gate to ask alms of those entering the temple."

questions.q: When Peter entered the house of Cornelius, the Roman centurion fell down at his feet to worship him. How did Peter correct him? (Acts 10:25-26)
options: He accepted the worship because he was the head apostle.
He lifted him up, saying, "Stand up; I too am a man."
He demanded that Cornelius bring an offering first.
He was offended and walked out of the house.
questions.explain: Peter completely rejected being treated as a deity or higher being, stating humbly: "Stand up; I too am a man." This reinforced that only God should be worshipped.

questions.q: In the early church, when Stephen was arrested and brought before the council, the false witnesses claimed he spoke words against the temple and the law. However, what did all who sat in the council notice about Stephen's face? (Acts 6:15)
options: It looked dark and extremely angry.
It looked like the face of an angel.
It was covered in tears of fear.
It became aged and completely white.
questions.explain: Despite being falsely accused and on trial for his life, Acts 6:15 notes: "And gazing at him, all who sat in the council saw that his face was like the face of an angel," reflecting the peace and presence of the Holy Spirit.
